D010-D006_h001.question:
It kind of feels like my whole life’s been split in two this past year.  

About seven months ago I hit this…high. For like two months straight I barely slept and didn’t even feel tired. I was always on the move—doing extra delivery shifts, then coming home and pacing or going for long drives at 2 a.m. My mood was all over the place; one minute I’d be on top of the world, joking, laughing, and the next I’d snap at people over nothing. My coworkers couldn’t keep up with how fast I was talking—I’d jump from one topic to another and it felt physically uncomfortable to shut up.  

I got super focused on sex too—hookup apps nonstop, risky stuff I wouldn’t usually do. I even put a bunch of money I don’t really have into this sketchy “delivery startup” some guy on Discord pitched me, didn’t really read anything, just wired it.  

During that time I also became convinced my ex was cheating on me, even though we weren’t even together. I kept “seeing” guys standing near her car or outside my apartment—full-on people, then they’d just vanish. That only happened during that high phase.  

Then I crashed. For the last five months I’ve just felt flat and low. I don’t enjoy anything—music, games, even driving feels pointless. I can’t decide on simple stuff like what to eat, so I just skip meals. I’m calling in sick, missing shifts. I’m not seeing things or having those cheating thoughts anymore, just this heavy, empty feeling that won’t lift.
D010-D006_h001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D010-D006_h001.answer: A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h002.question:
It’s been a really strange year. Around last winter I hit this low that lasted for months—like five months straight. I just felt…flattened. I’d go to the lab and stare at code or data and my brain felt full of fog, like I couldn’t hold a thought long enough to finish an email, let alone an analysis pipeline. I started ducking out of lab meetings, ignoring Slack messages, avoiding friends’ texts. My husband kept asking what was wrong and I just didn’t have the energy to care or explain. I wasn’t crying all the time, it was more this heavy, gray, “what’s the point” feeling.

Then it suddenly flipped, almost like someone threw a switch. For about two months I felt wired all the time—sleep didn’t seem necessary, I was constantly pacing or cleaning, starting new projects at 2 a.m. I was talking nonstop, even in meetings, interrupting people, messaging collaborators at all hours. I became weirdly social, reaching out to old colleagues, trying to organize meetups and side projects.

During that time I became convinced something was seriously wrong inside my body—like my organs were decaying or infected, even though tests were normal. I kept tasting this metallic, chemical flavor in my mouth out of nowhere, certain it meant my insides were rotting. Those beliefs and tastes only happened during that “high” period, never before or after. My work and home life really fell apart in both phases.
D010-D006_h002.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Adjustment Disorder
D010-D006_h002.answer: A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D010-D006_h003.question:

D010-D006_h006.question:

I can’t sit still, I pace the unit, start multiple tasks at once. My coworkers say I talk so fast they can’t get a word in. During this time I’ve been convinced something is wrong inside my body, like my organs are rotting, and I hear a voice commenting on it, telling me my insides are damaged.
